source.figure_namespace: NIST NCSTAR 1-9, Chapter 5; physical PDF page is one-based; printed page = physical page - 44 for these pages
source.ceiling: What the preserved report attributes to its embedded imagery; camera-original files, calibration, capture times and historical authenticity are not independently established.

method.page_display: Existing full-page 935 x 1210 PNGs; original report captions, footers, in-image credits and placement reviewed. Text-only supplementary pages are explicitly distinguished from visually reviewed pages.
method.blinding_limit: This source reviewer saw report captions and imagery together and did not label appearance. No new root or second-reviewer labels were read. Prior review files were used for ID-set subtraction and protocol limitations only.

shared_caveats.attribution: Report describes sporadic/variable coverage, nearby building obstruction of lower floors, dust, smoke, distance and access limits, especially scarce lower-floor imagery near the last hour.

Only some camera clocks tied to known events; other times use shadows and fire-window positions with substantial uncertainty. Claimed time precision is not universally equivalent to independent clock evidence.

Report coding separates no visible fire from not observable and uses unknown code 9 for smoke obscuration, insufficient resolution or lack of a suitable image. Fire, smoke and open-window observations are not independent.
Section 5.6.3 says limited imagery makes detailed four-face fire timelines difficult.
No available images of certain faces/floors/times is not an observed absence of hidden fire; the same page says smoke could suggest lower-floor fires without identifying originating windows.
Existing caption prints 12:28 a.m. +/- 3 min while surrounding sequence says p.m.; original contradiction retained in inventory.
